The Knighting Ceremony is meant to be a ritual timed appropriately to allow reflection and to celebrate your outgrowth from mentorship, but we realize that you were hurried through this process and that you might need some time to find your path.|Adi Gallia and Iskat Akaris|<ref name="Rise of the Red Blade" />}}
Adi Gallia was a female Tholothian,<ref name="Adi Gallia DB" /> a seemingly ageless<ref name="Alien Archive" /> near-human species.<ref name="UP">''[[Unlimited Power]]''</ref> She had [[Color|blue]] [[eye]]s, dark skin mottled with blue pigment, particularly around her eyes,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and stood at 1.74 [[meter]]s, or 5 [[Foot|feet]] and 9 [[Rob Inch|inches]].<ref name="Join the Battle" /> Although not a native of Tholoth,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> the homeworld of the Tholothians,<ref name="UP" /> Gallia was still a biological Tholothian and, as such, had a scaled cranium. From this skullcap, eight fleshy head tendrils, which were white with speckled coloration, descended to her shoulders.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

[[File:AdiGallia-SWE.png|thumb|left|220px|Adi Gallia's greatest assets were her intelligence and political acumen, and she would later be a capable combatant.]]
Born into the high-class political scene of Coruscant's ecumenopolis, Gallia experienced a wide range of worldviews in her youth, beginning with the wealth and formalities her parents' occupations afforded her. Though taken to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant at a young age, Gallia remembered her former social life well and missed the closeness that she felt was lacking in the Temple. As a Jedi trainee, she routinely escaped the haunting, brooding atmosphere of the Temple to explore her homeworld, excursions that she considered brought her closer to the realities of civilian life. Though once the auspicious child of upper-class diplomats, Gallia had no issue wandering between the many levels of Coruscant's cityscape and could blend into the varied social classes with ease. Her experiences freely roaming Coruscant impacted her outlook and opinions, and she adopted egalitarian stances on policy and strategy, positions that gave her word value to the Jedi High Council since they offered new perspectives to the body.<ref name="Force Users" />

As a member of the Jedi Council, Gallia also proved different to her peers for her penchant for behind-the-scenes work. Believing that information was more effective than a lightsaber in almost all circumstances, Gallia used her class awareness and political acumen to establish a network of spies and informants. Highly respected and revered for her intelligence and powers of intuition, Gallia was able to provide her colleagues with a new source of information and mold herself into a leading beacon of the Council,<ref name="Force Users" /> which brought her into the circles of<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> progressive politicians<ref name="SWCT Organa">{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Bail Organa - Galactic Senate}}</ref> such as Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum and Senator Bail Organa.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Since childhood, Gallia had valued the efficacy of political strategy and found that she excelled in information gathering and high politics.<ref name="Force Users" /> Though known mostly for her intelligence,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Gallia was also known for her infamous cynicism.<ref name="Tales from Vader's Castle 2" /> She had a sarcastic wit<ref name="GI" /> and a cynical attitude,<ref name="Tales from Vader's Castle 2" /> even towards her fellow Jedi,<ref name="Adi Gallia DB" /> both of which were qualities that made her appear standoffish and were commented on by the likes of Grand Master Yoda.<ref name="Tales from Vader's Castle 2" />

[[File:CitadelRescueJedi.png|thumb|right|330px|Proving to be an excellent military commander, Gallia took part in strategizing various battles during the Clone Wars.]]
Most at home while dealing with Coruscant's political spheres, Gallia was a peaceful being, but the outbreak of the Clone Wars abruptly threw her onto the battlefield as a Jedi General, a title she was uncomfortable accepting. Despite her initial hesitancy, Gallia, who was used to changing her lifestyle to fit her needs,<ref name="Force Users" /> was able to make the transition from a peacekeeper into a wartime commander easily<ref name="AdiGalliaSWE" /> and helped strategize the earliest stages of the war effort. Although Gallia believed that it was the Jedi's duty to do as they were called to in service of the Republic, she felt that the Order had made unwise decisions to promote unprepared Padawans to Knighthood for the sole purpose of sending them into battle, which she believed made some of the new Jedi Knights, such as Akaris, unsure of themselves and lacking a well-developed internal compass.<ref name="Rise of the Red Blade" /> The war likewise forced Gallia herself to alter her ways and become a dedicated warrior, an aspect of being a Jedi she had put aside to focus on her information brokering.<ref name="Force Users" />

On the front, Gallia improved her combat skills enough<ref name="Force Users" /> that she earned a reputation for aggression and her willingness to bring the fight to the Separatists. Stern and focused, she was unaccustomed to the outrageous tactics of Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi, but she rarely condemned their actions due to their effectiveness,<ref name="SWCT">{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Adi Gallia - Jedi Master}}</ref> as well as how entertaining she sometimes found them.<ref name="AdiGalliaSWE" /> Although the by-the-books<ref name="Rise of the Red Blade" /> Gallia did not see eye-to-eye with Skywalker tactically, she appreciated his quick thinking and decisiveness in combat. Her amusement at Skywalker's recklessness<ref name="Join the Battle" /> was not shared with those she believed had not earned the ability to speak their mind, including Akaris, who she was quick to shut down despite her sympathy for the young woman.<ref name="Rise of the Red Blade" /> As the war dragged on, Gallia proved herself to be an effective general. Long sympathetic to Kenobi for the death of his master and her friend, Qui-Gon Jinn,<ref name="Force Users" /> who shared her preoccupation with class issues,<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /> Gallia nobly offered to aid his hunt for Jinn's killer, a choice that would lead to her death at the hands of Savage Opress.<ref name="Force Users" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Master Gallia, you go ahead. I'll get Eeth back to the shuttle.''"<br />"''May the Force be with you.|Anakin Skywalker urges Adi Gallia to fight General Grievous|<ref name="GI" />}}
[[File:BattleMeditation-SWZ.png|thumb|left|330px|Attuned to the Force, Master Gallia employed the power of battle meditation, including while in-flight.]]
Like all Jedi, Gallia received training in lightsaber combat,<ref name="SOTJ">''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Jedi]]''</ref> but her concentration on operating her covert intelligence network on Coruscant after rising to a position on the High Council meant she was not a dedicated lightsaber duelist. When forced into action as a General of the Republic Army during the Clone Wars, Gallia had to improve her abilities<ref name="Force Users" /> and soon proved an aggressive warrior on the battlefront.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> A user of [[Form V]],<ref name="AEYNTK">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''</ref> a variant of [[Form III]] that focused on incorporating both defensive and offensive tactics,<ref name="KoF">''[[Knights of Fate]]''</ref> Gallia's lightsaber style was acrobatic and made good use of her limber physique.<ref name="Lightsaber Guide">''[[Star Wars Lightsabers: A Guide to Weapons of the Force]]''</ref> During the war, she dueled the feared General Grievous twice and held her own despite failing to outright defeat him either time. Though Gallia was able to hone her duelling skills, she still demonstrated difficulty meeting the attacks of a sith apprentice. Against Savage Opress head on, Gallia was not prepared, having to evade and backpedal from his furious and unconventional double bladed offensive. Gallia's inferior strength against her opponent, coupled with being unable to intercept his overwhelming force attack, led to her death .<ref name="Force Users" />

Among Gallia's other abilities, she was recognized for her [[pilot]]ing skills as an expert starfighter pilot,<ref name="Join the Battle" /> which proved vital to the space battles she was involved in throughout the Clone Wars,<ref name="CR" /> such as Geonosis<ref name="Force Users" /> and Lola Sayu.<ref name="CR" /> Naturally attuned to the Force from a young age,<ref name="Force Users" /> Gallia was adept at using telekinesis,<ref name="Tales from Vader's Castle 2" /> a talent honed during her Jedi training,<ref name="SOTJ" /> and was able to use the power of [[Battle meditation|Battle Meditation]]<ref name="X-Wing">{{FFGXW2|set=Delta-7 Aethersprite Expansion Pack|cardname=Battle Meditation}}</ref> and the [[mind trick]].<ref name="Jedi Knights 1">[[Jedi Knights 1|''Jedi Knights'' 1]]</ref> She was also an agile fighter, and she could nimbly dodge attacks<ref name="Revival" /> and make quick movements and counterattacks in the heat of battle.<ref name="Nomad Droids" /> Gallia was widely celebrated for her intelligence<ref name="Pocket" /> and diplomatic abilities, proving herself a capable political advisor<ref name="Force Users" /> as well as a naval commander; during the Clone Wars, she was able to make critical decisions quickly, for instance swiftly ordering the evacuation of her flagship when under attack during the Battle of Patitite Pattuna,<ref name="Nomad Droids" /> a choice that allowed many of the clones under her command to survive and regroup.<ref name="HC 33" />

==Equipment==
[[File:AdiGalliaDelta7B-TCWs3BR3.png|thumb|right|225px|Adi Gallia piloting her Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]]
Over the course of her long career as a Jedi, Master Gallia wielded two lightsabers. After her first was lost on a mission prior to the Invasion of Naboo, she replaced it with a new lightsaber that she would wield for the rest of her life.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" /> A single-blade lightsaber that emitted blue [[plasma]] from its central [[kyber crystal]],<ref name="Lightsaber Guide" /> Gallia used the lightsaber in many battles and duels during the Clone Wars, including against opponents such as Grievous and Savage Opress.<ref name="Force Users" /> The weapon's hilt was identical to that of fellow Jedi Council members Shaak Ti and Agen Kolar- made from durasteel components and measuring 26.6 centimeters in length.<ref name="Lightsaber Guide" /> Another of Gallia's personal equipment was her Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor. Manufactured by [[Kuat Systems Engineering]], the Delta 7B was a variant of the Delta 7 and was the common starfighter used by the Jedi Order.<ref name="USW" /> Equipped with an astromech droid co-pilot, Gallia's starfighter was given a red-and-white paint scheme with the [[Republic crest]] displayed on its wing.<ref name="CR" />

As a Jedi Master, Gallia wore an [[Jedi apparel|outfit commonly worn]] among members of the Order, a tunic and accompanying robe with simple, neutral and non aggressive colours. In addition, she wore simple blue-grey pants and tall, rust coloured travel [[boot]]s, and on her belt was a utility pouch held together by a square buckle. Like her cousin, Stass Allie, Gallia wore a traditional [[Tholoth headdress|Tholothian headdress]], characteristically consisting of a scaled cranium and pale, fleshy tendrils hanging limply toward the shoulders .<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> During the Clone Wars, when many Jedi adopted the white-plated [[armor]] developed on Kamino for the clone armies, Gallia began wearing forearm armor previously utilized by the [[Coruscant Guard]].<ref name="Brotherhood" /> Like her fellow Jedi, Gallia<ref name="Join the Battle" /> accommodated their Jedi robes for the changes,<ref name="Brotherhood" /> with her sleeves tucked into her armor, adorned with the Coruscant Guard's symbol, at the elbow.<ref name="Join the Battle" />However when accompanying her friend Obi-Wan on the mission to Bray, She did wear full body armour in addition to her tunic and robe.

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|It said sort of African, South African, regal, right? And so, I looked at it, and I was like, 'I don't do South African.' And, um, I always say that the way I got this role is by spending the night with Don Cheadle.|Angelique Perrin, on auditioning for the role of Adi Gallia|<ref name="Conversations">{{YouTube|video=593xsRyAfyU|text=Clone Wars Conversations Ep 10: Angelique Perrin "More than a Jedi"|channel=@JamesArnoldTaylor|name=James Arnold Taylor}}</ref>}}
Adi Gallia first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], where she was portrayed by [[Gin Clarke]], credited only as "Gin."<ref name="Episode I" /> For the sequel to ''The Phantom Menace'', [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], Clarke was unable to reprise the role and the casting department for the film began searching for someone to replace her. In their search, the casting directors came across [[Lily Nyamwasa]], a model who resembled Clarke. At their request, Nyamwasa went to [[Fox Studios, Sydney|Fox Studios]] to try on Clarke's headpiece for Gallia, which fit perfectly, but her appearance was noticeably different than Clarke's. Because of the difference in appearance, ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator and ''Attack of the Clones'' director [[George Lucas]] decided to cast Nyamwasa as Adi Gallia's cousin, "Stass Allie," rather than have Nyamwasa portray Gallia herself. Though Lucas decided not to recast Gallia,<ref name="Nyamwasa Interview">{{WebCite|url=https://starwarsinterviews.com/prequel-trilogy/episode-ii-attack-of-the-clones/lily-nyamwasa-stass-allie|text=Lily Nyamwasa (Stass Allie)|author=[[Dennis Pellegrom]]|date=2006|work=[[Star Wars Interviews]]|archivedate=20230205201431}}</ref> stock footage of Clarke's portrayal of her from ''The Phantom Menace'' was recycled as part of new Jedi High Council scenes.<ref name="Episode II" />

[[File:AngeliquePerrin.png|thumb|left|220px|Adi Gallia is voiced in ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' by Angelique Perrin.]]
Gallia is featured in the [[2008]] animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''<ref name="GI" /> as a recurring part of the supporting cast. In ''The Clone Wars'', Gallia is voiced by actress [[Angelique Perrin]]. Perrin, a lifelong ''Star Wars'' fan, was first sent information about the role by her agent. As was the case with many casting calls made for ''The Clone Wars'', the casting sheet did not specify the character and, according to Perrin, only requested an actor who could portray a "sort of African, South African, regal" voice. Though initially wary of agreeing to audition because she did not believe she could do a [[wikipedia:South Africa|South African]] accent, Perrin spent the night watching the [[2004]] film [[wikipedia: Hotel Rwanda|''Hotel Rwanda'']], in which actor [[wikipedia:Don Cheadle|Don Cheadle]] uses a South African accent, and by the next morning recorded her audition without hesitation and was later informed that she had landed the job.<ref name="Conversations" /> For ''The Clone Wars'', Gallia was designed in part by [[Darren Marshall]], who created a stylized maquette of Gallia's head for reference and concept art of the character.<ref name="GI Episode Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/grievous-intrigue-concept-art-gallery|text="Grievous Intrigue" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slide 1}}</ref>

The first episode of ''The Clone Wars'' in which Gallia appears is "[[Grievous Intrigue]]," the ninth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]], which was directed by [[Giancarlo Volpe]], written by [[Ben Edlund]], [[Drew Z. Greenberg]], and [[Brian Larsen]], and released on [[January 1]], [[2010]].<ref name="GI EpGuide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode209.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Grievous Intrigue}}</ref> In a rare moment for the show, Gallia was scripted to say the famous ''Star Wars'' line "[[May the Force be with you]]" by series director [[Dave Filoni]]. Though Filoni believed that George Lucas would remove it when reviewing the script, Lucas left it in. While recording the episode, Perrin stopped the session to express her excitement despite it being her first time recording with the cast, and as a result, the session was delayed when she and the rest of the crew discussed the line and its importance. Soon after "Grievous Intrigue" aired, Perrin began receiving mail from fans of ''The Clone Wars'', which she felt cemented herself as a ''Star Wars'' actor.<ref name="Conversations" /> Perrin reprised the role in four more episodes, [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|season three]]'s "[[Witches of the Mist]]"<ref name="WotM" /> and "[[Citadel Rescue]],"<ref name="CR" /> [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|season four]]'s "[[Nomad Droids]],"<ref name="Nomad Droids" /> and [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|season five]]'s "[[Revival]]."<ref name="Revival" />

By the time of the recording of "Revival," the creative team behind ''The Clone Wars'' had ceased sending actors scripts prior to the sessions, and Perrin was unaware that Gallia would be killed off in the episode until the day of recording. While reading the script, Perrin first missed the action line indicating that Gallia would be killed. Upon re-reading the script and realizing her character would be dying she became emotional in her recording booth, but later appreciated that Gallia "went out with a bang."<ref name="Conversations" /> Perrin, alongside several other ''Clone Wars'' veterans, reprised her role for a voice cameo in the [[2019]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']], in which Gallia is one of the "Voices of Jedi Past" who speak to Rey during the film's climax.<ref name="Episode IX" /> The actors who reprised their characters were only called in the weeks before the film's release on [[December 20]], [[2019]], and were given the same set of lines to record. Although the returning actors had to record in secret, rumors swirled that there were actors brought in to film appearances as Force ghosts.<ref name="IX Cameo">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/freddie-prinze-jr-shares-the-story-behind-kanans-cameo-in-star-wars-the-rise-of-skywalker|text=Freddie Prinze Jr Shares the Story Behind Kanan's Cameo in Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker|author=Yehl, Joshua|date=2020-02-13|archivedate=20200305170105}}</ref>

===Contradictions===
There are two conflicting sources regarding Gallia's home world: ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' claims she hails from Tholoth,<ref name="USW" /> while ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''<ref name="AEYNTK" /> and ''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' both state that she is from Coruscant.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> At the same time, the old [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]] on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="AdiGalliaSWE" /> and ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' listed Gallia's height as 1.74 meters.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> ''Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded'' says she stands at 1.84 meters.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Although the Encyclopedia on StarWars.com is no longer readily available, this article assumes the newer source, that being ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!'', is correct.
